$comment: P69 D-FFI-FCNTL-AARCH64-OPEN-FLAGS-TAKE-X86-64-VALUES. <fcntl.h>'s O_DIRECTORY, O_NOFOLLOW and O_TMPFILE differ by ARCH on Linux (arm64's uapi fcntl.h overrides asm-generic's, which x86_64 uses), and fcntl.json keyed them by format alone, so aarch64 took x86_64's values. Each target's expectedStdout is the REFERENCE's own run of this very source: gcc 13.3.0 -std=gnu2x on glibc 2.39, x86_64 (run 20260930-185033-96764b3e) and aarch64 native (run 20260930-185048-034f78bc), and Apple clang 21 on arm64 and x86_64 (run 20260930-184953-72badbea); O_TMPFILE, which glibc declares only under _GNU_SOURCE, was measured the same way with it (runs 20260930-175639-f43a1fd8 / 20260930-175657-9088f3f4). The BEHAVIOUR is the independent witness: a regular file opened with O_DIRECTORY must fail ENOTDIR and a symlink opened with O_NOFOLLOW must fail ELOOP (errno 40 on Linux, 62 on Darwin). RED-ON-DISABLE: the aarch64 arms reverted to x86_64's values make the aarch64 file cell open (0x10000 is arm64's O_DIRECT) and the link cell follow the link, so linux-arm64 exits 1 and prints errno 0 while x86_64 stays green (the control). No pe target: the UCRT declares none of these flags.

targets.expectedStdout:
O_DIRECTORY=0x10000 O_NOFOLLOW=0x20000 O_TMPFILE=0x410000
dir=opened file_errno=20 link_errno=40
